claims.text: Kardashev classified hypothetical civilizations by available power. Original Type I is approximately 4e12 W, Type II 4e26 W, Type III 4e37 W (1 erg/s = 1e-7 W).
claims.limitations: Historical order-of-magnitude classification, not evidence that Types II or III exist. Do not silently replace original Type I by a later planetary convention.

claims.text: Use the explicit mathematical convention K = (log10(P in W) - 6)/10: K=1,2,3 at 1e16,1e26,1e36 W.
claims.limitations: Commonly attributed to Sagan; original book passage/page remains unverified here. This convention differs from original 1964 values and does not measure ethics or human worth.

claims.text: Energy is measured in J; power in W=J/s. Annual EJ divided by the actual year duration gives an average power proxy. Total energy supply, final energy, electricity and useful exergy are different boundaries.
claims.limitations: Avoid double counting conversion inputs and electricity outputs; no cross-edition trend without harmonized accounting.

claims.text: Energy Institute reports 592 EJ total energy supply for 2024. With 366 days, CORE calculates about 18.72 TW and K about 0.727 under the stated proxy/convention.
claims.limitations: Not a current 2026 measurement, not useful work, not uncertainty bounds. Plus/minus 10% CLI scenarios are assumptions, not confidence intervals. Edition/accounting revisions need review.

claims.text: Usable work depends on source/sink conditions; dissipative energy use produces waste heat. Radiation-based engineering has efficiency and observational constraints.
claims.limitations: No universal engineering efficiency assigned. Exergy is not identical to energy; no waste-heat climate prediction computed here.

claims.text: Planetary-boundary research treats climate, ecosystems and other Earth systems as interacting constraints. The 2023 study reported six of nine boundaries transgressed.
claims.limitations: Historical assessment, not a current count. Thresholds and uncertainty are domain-specific; more power alone cannot certify sustainability.

claims.text: Energy pathways involve demand reduction, efficiency, renewables, nuclear, storage, transmission and grid flexibility, with physical, environmental and institutional tradeoffs.
claims.limitations: No technology is declared universally optimal; life-cycle impacts, siting, costs, materials and system boundaries require local evidence. No deployment recommendation or timetable.

claims.text: Dyson swarms and stellar-scale energy collection are hypothetical engineering/technosignature research subjects, not demonstrated CORE capabilities.
claims.limitations: Orbital dynamics, construction mass, propulsion, radiative balance, maintenance and light-travel constraints remain unresolved. No solid shell, faster-than-light travel or installed space industry claimed.

claims.text: Fermi/Great Filter arguments depend on uncertain occurrence rates, detectability, lifetimes and priors. Infrared excess alone does not establish extraterrestrial engineering.
claims.limitations: No probability of civilizational collapse or confirmed technosignature inferred. Later Type IV/V or multiverse extensions are speculative, outside tested physics here.

claims.text: CORE research should retain separate energy/exergy, ecology, wellbeing, peace/freedom/cooperation, resilience and scientific-capacity dimensions, with provenance and dissent for each.
claims.limitations: Founder-directed research framework, not an empirical composite index. No weights, country ranking, social score or single civilization score approved. Peace/freedom/resilience metrics and independent reviewers remain to be selected.
